title: Simulation Task
description: Develop a multi-agent simulation system that models the spread of mask-wearing behavior through social networks.
simulation_focus: Predict agents' mask-wearing behavior over day 30 - day 39 (last ten days) based on their attributes, social connections, and past behavior
Model information propagation and behavioral changes triggered by social influence and government intervention starting on Day 10

data_files.agent_attributes.csv: Contains demographic and behavioral attributes of each agent, including age, occupation, risk perception, and social connection counts
data_files.social_network.json: Contains structured data representing a social network. Each entry corresponds to a user (identified by a unique integer ID), and the values describe the different types of relationships that user has with others. Data Structure: The top-level structure is a dictionary ({} in JSON). Keys: Each key is a unique user ID (as an integer, e.g., 0, 1, 2, etc.). Values: Each value is another dictionary with the following fields: "family": a list of user IDs representing family connections. "work_school": a list of user IDs representing colleagues or schoolmates. "community": a list of user IDs representing community-level acquaintances. "all": a merged list of all user IDs connected to the user across the three categories above.
data_files.train_data.csv: Time series data for the first 30 days, used for training the model

RMSE.description: Root Mean Square Error measuring overall predictive accuracy of mask adoption rates
RMSE.interpretation: Directly interpretable as percentage deviations due to the 0-1 range

interactions.name: peer_influence
interactions.description: Agents observe neighbors' mask use and adjust their own adoption probability based on social conformity and perceived norms.

interactions.name: policy_mandate_compliance
interactions.description: Policies (mandates, enforcement, fines, subsidies) modify agents' perceived cost/benefit and compliance probability.

interactions.name: information_campaign_exposure
interactions.description: Agents receive messages from information sources that shift risk perception and adoption propensity depending on credibility and reach.

interactions.name: market_supply_constraint
interactions.description: Availability and price of masks affect agents' ability and willingness to adopt or maintain usage.

interactions.name: social_sharing
interactions.description: Agents share pro/anti-mask opinions which influence neighbors' info exposure and adoption decisions.

metrics.name: RMSE_of_adoption
metrics.description: Root Mean Squared Error between simulated and observed population mask adoption over the calibration period.

metrics.name: MAE_of_adoption
metrics.description: Mean Absolute Error between simulated and observed adoption time series.

metrics.name: R2_of_adoption
metrics.description: Coefficient of determination between simulated and observed adoption levels.

metrics.name: Peak_timing_error_days
metrics.description: Absolute difference in days between observed peak adoption and simulated peak adoption.

metrics.name: Final_adoption_gap
metrics.description: Absolute difference between observed and simulated adoption on the final day of the calibration period.

validation_criteria.name: Convergence_criterion
validation_criteria.description: Calibration terminates when improvement in the target metric across iterations falls below a tolerance for N successive iterations.

validation_criteria.name: Parameter_bounds_respected
validation_criteria.description: All calibrated parameters remain within specified prior bounds.

validation_criteria.name: Goodness_of_fit_threshold
validation_criteria.description: Accept calibrated model if target metric (e.g., RMSE_of_adoption) is below a pre-specified threshold.

validation_criteria.name: Stability_check
validation_criteria.description: Simulated adoption does not exhibit unrealistic oscillations or divergence under small perturbations.
